title: Story Game: how one activity connects the whole codebase
intro: Story Game (activities/story_game/story_game.py) is a make-believe storytelling game. Gigi greets the child, looks for a toy with the camera (YOLO), confirms it by listening (speech-to-text) and, if needed, asking the LLM, and then takes turns with the child telling a story until the child says "the end". One short script ends up using the camera, the microphone, the LLM, text-to-speech, the face screen, the motors and the logger, so it is a good tour of how the pieces fit together.

lifelines.name: Child
lifelines.desc: The person playing with Gigi: speaks into the microphone and holds toys up to the camera.

lifelines.name: Launcher
lifelines.desc: Starts the activity: either a developer in a terminal, or the always-running daemon (ExecutionManager) when the phone app asks for it.

lifelines.name: story_game.py
lifelines.desc: The activity script itself. Contains the game logic and a few helpers (object detection, confirmation parsing, response cleaning).

lifelines.name: Character
lifelines.desc: The facade (alias GigiRobot). Owns every subsystem and offers high-level verbs: run_character (speak + move + animate), listen_backchannel, lookat_something, log_variable ...

lifelines.name: Speech · Viseme
lifelines.desc: Text-to-speech (Nix-TTS on the robot, Silero on Windows), audio playback through pygame, and the viseme (mouth-shape) sequence that drives lip-sync.

lifelines.name: Face
lifelines.desc: Draws Gigi's animated face on the screen (pygame or OpenCV window): idle, blink, smile, lip-synced mouth ...

lifelines.name: Movement
lifelines.desc: Gestures and gaze. Turns named gestures (gesture_definitions.py) into smooth motor trajectories and sends PWM to the PCA9685 servo board over I²C. Robot only (HAS_MOVEMENT = IS_ROBOT).

lifelines.name: Hearing
lifelines.desc: Microphone capture, voice-activity detection (webrtcvad) and speech-to-text (SenseVoice on the NPU, or faster-whisper on a PC). Results are appended to hearing.texts.

lifelines.name: Vision
lifelines.desc: Camera capture and processing threads: face detection & recognition, emotion, gestures. Exposes the latest frame and per-face data (offset, name ...).

lifelines.name: Conversation
lifelines.desc: Talks to the LLM server over HTTP. get_response() is a stateless single turn (with optional RAG context); _call_npu() posts a raw message list.

lifelines.name: Logger
lifelines.desc: InteractionLogger: buffers conversation, visuals and variables, and writes them to data/users/<user>/<activity>/ once the user is recognised.

lifelines.name: LLM server
lifelines.desc: External process. On the robot: RKLLM (Qwen) on the NPU at :8080. On a PC: Ollama (llama3.2) at :11434. Chosen by config.IS_ROBOT.

phases.title: Launch
phases.summary: Two ways in: a developer runs the module from a terminal, or the phone app asks the always-running daemon to start it as a child process.

steps.label: process_command_line('run story_game')
steps.note: the app's command arrives over TCP, WebSocket, Bluetooth or serial
steps.detail: The daemon (core/daemon.py) runs permanently on the robot and listens on several transports. Every incoming line is handed to process_command_line(), which parses commands like 'run story_game'. Before running an activity it checks that the motors are calibrated.

steps.label: find_script('story_game') → path
steps.detail: find_script() maps the short activity name to a Python file inside src/gigi/activities.

steps.label: ExecutionManager.start_script() → subprocess.Popen([python, -u, story_game.py])
steps.note: the activity runs in its own process
steps.detail: ExecutionManager stops whatever is currently running (e.g. ambient 'alive mode') and launches the activity as a separate Python process. A monitor thread streams its stdout/stderr into the daemon log and waits for it to exit (see phase 6).

steps.label: or, from a terminal: python -m gigi.activities.story_game.story_game
steps.detail: During development you can skip the daemon and run the module directly. Both paths end up in play_story_game(), the single entry point of this activity.

phases.title: Setup: load YOLO, build the Character, start the camera
phases.summary: The game loads its own object detector, then creates a Character, which in turn builds every subsystem. Finally the camera threads are started.

steps.label: download_model_if_needed() → Resources/yolo11n.onnx
steps.detail: The YOLO11-nano ONNX model (~22 MB) is downloaded from Hugging Face on first use and cached in the Resources directory (config.RESOURCES_DIR).

steps.label: net = cv2.dnn.readNetFromONNX(YOLO_MODEL_PATH)
steps.detail: Object detection is owned by the game, not by the Vision subsystem: OpenCV's DNN module loads the network once and the game runs it on frames it pulls from Vision (phase 3).

steps.label: Character('fuzzy', wakeup=True, activity='StoryQuest')
steps.note: one constructor builds the whole robot
steps.detail: Character (alias GigiRobot) is the facade of the codebase. Its constructor checks the HAS_* flags in core/config.py and creates each subsystem shown in the next steps. Activities normally talk only to this object.

steps.label: Face() · generate_face(basic_sequences['idle'])
steps.detail: Opens the face window and shows the idle face for the chosen character ('fuzzy').

steps.label: Speech() loads TTS · Viseme(face, speech)
steps.detail: Speech loads the text-to-speech model (Nix-TTS on the robot, Silero on Windows) and initialises the pygame mixer. Viseme links Speech and Face so the mouth can follow the audio.

steps.label: Movement() → PCA9685Controller() · home_position()
steps.detail: On the robot, Movement opens the PCA9685 PWM board over I²C and moves every servo to its home pose. On a PC this subsystem is None and all movement calls are skipped.

steps.label: Hearing() loads STT + webrtcvad
steps.detail: Speech-to-text: SenseVoice on the NPU (RKNN) when USE_NPU_TRANSCRIPTION is set, otherwise faster-whisper. webrtcvad is used for voice-activity detection.

steps.label: Vision() → FaceDatabase, EmotionDetector, ImprovedFaceCache
steps.detail: Vision prepares the face database (known people), the emotion detector and a face cache that keeps identities stable across frames. The helpers live in vision_helper.py.

steps.label: SpeakerDatabase() + voice encoder
steps.detail: Speaker identification: a voice-embedding model (RKNN on the robot) plus a small database of known voices. Used later while listening to find out who is talking.

steps.label: Conversation() picks the LLM URL from config.IS_ROBOT
steps.detail: On the robot the LLM is RKLLM on the NPU (port 8080); on a PC it is Ollama (port 11434).

steps.label: InteractionLogger()
steps.detail: Logs are buffered in memory until the user is recognised, then written to data/users/<user>/<activity>/.

steps.label: gigi.vision.run_vision()
steps.note: the game reaches past the facade into a subsystem
steps.detail: Instead of a Character method, the game calls the Vision object directly. This works, but it couples the activity to Vision's API. Notice the orange arrows: they mark every place where the facade is bypassed.

steps.label: threads: _capture_loop() + _vision_loop() → _process_frame()
steps.detail: One thread reads frames from cv2.VideoCapture; another processes them (face detection, recognition, emotion ...) and stores the results that get_latest_frame() and get_last_data() return.

phases.title: Greeting: what every run_character(...) call does
phases.summary: Gigi says hello and waves. This is the anatomy of run_character(), the single call that makes Gigi speak, lip-sync and gesture at the same time. Every later 'Gigi says ...' repeats it.

steps.label: run_character({'text': 'Hi there! ...'}, movement_data='wave_hello')
steps.detail: The most used method of the codebase. It takes optional speech (viseme_data / audio_data), a gesture (movement_data), face, caption, image and video arguments, and runs them all in sync.

steps.label: log_conversation('Gigi', text)
steps.detail: Everything Gigi says is added to the activity log. If the text mentions a person Gigi knows (egocentric_db), she also turns to look at that person.

steps.label: update_audio_objects(text) → TTS → .wav · generate_viseme_sequence(text)
steps.detail: The audio is synthesised before anything starts playing, so that speech, mouth and gesture can start together. The viseme sequence (mouth shapes over time) is computed from the audio envelope.

steps.label: movement_thread('wave_hello').start()
steps.detail: Gestures run in their own thread so that Gigi can move while she talks.

steps.label: BASIC_GESTURES → smooth_sequence() → move_motors() → set_pwm() over I²C
steps.detail: Named gestures are keyframes in gesture_definitions.py. They are smoothed into a trajectory, converted to servo angles and finally to PWM duty cycles on the PCA9685 board.

steps.label: play_audio_thread().start() → speaker (pygame.mixer)
steps.detail: Playback runs in a thread and reports the exact moment audio started, which the face uses to stay in sync.

steps.label: combine_seuqences() · generate_face(start_time=audio start)
steps.detail: Face sequences (e.g. a requested expression plus the visemes) are merged, then drawn frame by frame, aligned to the audio start time. (The misspelled name combine_seuqences is the real method name.)

phases.title: Find the prop with the camera (up to 30 s)
phases.summary: Gigi asks the child to show a toy, then repeatedly grabs the latest camera frame and runs YOLO on it until something that is not a person shows up.

steps.label: holds a toy up to the camera
gigi.vision.get_latest_frame()
steps.detail: Called every 0.3 s for up to 30 s. Returns the most recent frame captured by Vision's capture thread.

steps.label: run_object_detection(net, frame) → YOLO11n + NMS → PROP_CLASSES[class_id]
steps.detail: The frame is resized to 640×640, passed through the network, filtered by confidence (> 0.40) and non-maximum suppression. People (COCO class 0) are ignored; the most confident remaining object is mapped to a friendly name via PROP_CLASSES (default 'toy'). If nothing is found in 30 s, Gigi asks for the toy's name instead.

phases.title: Confirm the prop: listening, with an LLM fallback
phases.summary: Gigi asks 'Is that what we are playing with?' and listens. listen_backchannel() is the second key facade method: it records and transcribes speech while keeping Gigi alive (tracking the face, blinking, identifying the speaker). If the child says no, the LLM extracts the toy's name.

steps.label: run_character('Oh! I see you brought a {prop}! ...')
get_user_input(gigi, 8) → gigi.listen_backchannel(timeout=8)
steps.detail: get_user_input() clears hearing.texts, listens for 8 seconds and joins whatever was transcribed. If Hearing is disabled it falls back to typing in the terminal.

steps.label: clear_audio_buffer() · hearing_thread(stop_event).start()
steps.detail: A timer sets stop_event after the timeout. If Vision is not running, listen_backchannel starts it (and stops it again at the end).

steps.label: _speaker_recognition_worker() thread: voice encoder → identify_speaker()
steps.detail: In parallel, the speaker's voice is embedded and matched against the SpeakerDatabase, so Gigi knows who is talking (and can look at them).

steps.label: listen(): audio_callback_optimized() → webrtcvad → transcribe_with_dedup() → texts
steps.detail: Audio chunks are collected, voice activity is detected, and each utterance is transcribed. Duplicated words and known STT hallucinations are removed before the text is appended to hearing.texts.

steps.label: get_last_data() (face offset)
steps.detail: While listening, Gigi keeps looking at the child: the horizontal offset of the detected face is read on every loop iteration.

steps.label: lookat_coordinate() → move_motors({torso, neck})
steps.detail: The face offset is converted to a target torso angle (using the look-at calibration if available) and split between torso and neck for a natural, damped motion.

steps.label: log_conversation(speaker, text)
steps.detail: When listening ends, the final transcription is stored under the recognised speaker (SpeakerDatabase) and in the conversation log.

steps.label: gigi.hearing.texts
steps.note: the game reads the transcript straight from the Hearing object

steps.label: parse_confirmation(text)
steps.detail: A simple keyword check for yes, yeah, yep, sure, correct, right, uh-huh ...

steps.label: if not confirmed: gigi.conversation.get_response('Extract the toy name…', text)
steps.detail: Gigi asks for the toy's name, listens again, and uses the LLM as a tiny information extractor. get_response() builds a fresh two-message prompt (adding RAG context if configured) and does not touch the conversation history.

steps.label: _call_npu() → HTTP POST (requests)
steps.detail: Sends {model, messages, stream: false} and reads choices[0].message.content. Note: on any error it does NOT raise; it returns a random 'timeout' phrase instead.

steps.label: clean_response(raw) → prop
steps.detail: story_game.py has its own clean_response() with the same idea (strip 'robot:' / 'gigi:' prefixes and extra dialogue), so the reply is cleaned twice.

phases.title: Story loop: repeat until the child says "the end"
phases.summary: Each turn: look at the child, listen, react with a filler, ask the LLM for the next sentence of the story, and say it with a random gesture. The whole history is sent to the LLM every time.

steps.label: look_and_stop('face') → look_for() → found['face']
steps.detail: look_for() starts a worker thread that searches the vision data for a face, while overlaying the camera feed on the face screen.
steps.warn: Bug: look_for() in vision.py still has 'from faceDefinitions import global_parts'. That module no longer exists (it is now gigi.expression.face_definitions), so this call raises ModuleNotFoundError. In Story Game the outer try/except catches it and the game ends at the first story turn.

steps.label: update_egocentric_locations() · stop_vision()
steps.detail: Remembers where people are around the robot, then stops the vision threads. The next listen_backchannel() call starts them again: a stop/restart on every turn.

steps.label: "...and then the dinosaur flew to the moon!"
finish phrase? ('the end', 'quit', 'bye bye' ...) → go to phase 6
steps.detail: If nothing was heard, Gigi says 'I'm listening!' and the loop restarts. Otherwise the child's sentence is appended to story_history.

steps.label: run_character(random filler, e.g. 'Oh! And then?')
steps.detail: A quick reaction hides the LLM latency.

steps.label: gigi.conversation._call_npu(story_history)
steps.detail: The game builds its own message list (a system prompt plus every turn so far) and calls the private _call_npu() helper, bypassing both the facade and Conversation's public API. Because _call_npu() swallows errors, the game's own except branch (a fallback sentence) rarely runs; on failure Gigi says a timeout phrase instead.

steps.label: clean_response() · keep first sentence · append to story_history
run_character(sentence, random gesture: open_arms / clap / look_from_side_to_side / home)

phases.title: Wrap-up and shutdown
phases.summary: Gigi celebrates, says goodbye and returns to her home pose. The finally block stops the camera and the face, flushes the logs, and the process exits; the daemon notifies the app.

steps.label: run_character('... The end! You are a great storyteller!', 'clap')
finally: gigi.vision.stop_vision()
steps.detail: Runs even if an exception ended the game early.

steps.label: flush buffers as guest 'Friend' if the user was never recognised
process exits → _monitor_lifecycle() → handle_completion_callback()
steps.detail: The daemon's monitor thread sees the exit code, sends a 'completed' event to the connected app, and, if ambient mode is enabled, resumes 'alive mode'.
